title: A2-21 · Travel, health and public offices

blocks.text: A2-21 · Travel, health and public offices
Lesson overview

Luca's gone. In this unit you follow him to Cairo airport, luggage office, hotel, doctor, pharmacy and language center counter. These are the situations in which a traveller must be understood with simple but precise phrases: ask with courtesy ( ⁧هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ⁩ …, ⁧أُرِيدُ أَنْ⁩ …, ⁧أَرْجُو أَنْ⁩ ...), describe an object or symptom, give your data, understand a warning and a form. The vocabulary is very concrete; grammar is what you know. Reading texts are without vowels, such as real alerts and forms. Two weeks.

rows: A2 · Module A2.4 Use the language
A2-20 exceeded; imperative and courtesy (A2-06); Numbers, dates and prices (A2-12)
12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 86–87 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-21), voice synthesis script, your passport or a real form (for terminology), session with the tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. making courteous and formal requests ( ⁧هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ⁩ …, ⁧مِنْ فَضْلِكَ⁩ , ⁧أَرْجُو أَنْ⁩ …, ⁧لَوْ سَمَحْتَ⁩ );
2. understand airport alerts and answer questions to passport control;
3. report lost baggage, book and register at the hotel;
4. describe to the doctor where it hurts, from when and how, and understand instructions for a drug;
5. fill out a form and solve a file at the counter.
Two-week plan.

blocks.text: 1. Dialogue 1 · On arrival
Cairo Airport, Saturday 11 July, afternoon. First passport control, then the lost luggage office.

rows: ⁧المُوَظَّف: جَوَازُ السَّفَرِ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. مَا سَبَبُ الزِّيَارَةِ؟⁩
al-muwaẓẓaf: ǧawāzu s-safar, min faḍlik. mā sababu z-ziyāra?
Your passport, please. What is the reason for the visit?
⁧لُوكَا: دِرَاسَةٌ. سَأَدْرُسُ العَرَبِيَّةَ فِي مَرْكَزٍ لِلُّغَاتِ فِي الدُّقِّي.⁩
Lūkā: dirāsa. sa-adrusu l-ʿarabiyyata fī markazin li-l-luġāti fī d-Duqqī.
Studio. I will study Arabic in a language center in Dokki.
al-muwaẓẓaf: kam yawman sa-tabqā? wa-ayna sa-tuqīm?
How many days will you stay? And where are you staying?
⁧لُوكَا: أُسْبُوعَيْنِ. سَأُقِيمُ فِي شَقَّةٍ، وَهٰذَا هُوَ العُنْوَانُ.⁩
Lūkā: usbūʿayn. sa-uqīmu fī šaqqa, wa-hāḏā huwa l-ʿunwān.
Two weeks. I'll stay in an apartment, and here's the address.
al-muwaẓẓaf: tafaḍḍal. ahlan bika fī Miṣr.
⁧بَعْدَ سَاعَةٍ، فِي مَكْتَبِ الأَمْتِعَةِ⁩ ) ⁧لُوكَا:⁩ . ⁧لَوْ سَمَحْتَ، حَقِيبَتِي لَمْ تَصِلْ⁩ ( ⁧المَفْقُودَةِ⁩
Lūkā: (baʿda sāʿa, fī maktabi l-amtiʿati l- mafqūda) law samaḥt, ḥaqībatī lam taṣil.
Luca: (An hour later, at the lost luggage office) Sorry, my suitcase didn't arrive.
⁧المُوَظَّفَة: مَا رَقْمُ رِحْلَتِكَ؟ وَهَلْ عِنْدَكَ قَسِيمَةُ الأَمْتِعَةِ؟⁩
al-muwaẓẓafa: mā raqmu riḥlatik? wa- hal ʿindaka qasīmatu l-amtiʿa?
The employee: What is the number of your flight? And do you have the luggage receipt?
⁧لُوكَا: نَعَمْ، تَفَضَّلِي. وَصَلْتُ مِنْ مِيلَانُو قَبْلَ سَاعَةٍ.⁩
Lūkā: naʿam, tafaḍḍalī. waṣaltu min Mīlānū qabla sāʿa.
Yes, there you go. I arrived from Milan an hour ago.
⁧حَقِيبَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ زَرْقَاءُ، ثَقِيلَةٌ جِدًّا، عَلَيْهَا⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧وَهَدِيَّةٌ لِعَمّ أَحْمَد.⁩ … ⁧اسْمِي. فِيهَا كُتُبٌ كَثِيرَةٌ⁩
Lūkā: ḥaqībatun kabīratun zarqāʾ, ṯaqīlatun ǧiddan, ʿalayhā smī. fīhā kutubun kaṯīra… wa-hadiyyatun li- ʿAmm Aḥmad.
Luca: A big and blue suitcase, very heavy, with my name on it. There are a lot of books inside... and a gift for ʿAmm Aḥmad.

blocks.text: al-muwaẓẓafa: yabdū annahā baqiyat The employee: It seems that she has stayed
⁧يَبْدُو أَنَّهَا بَقِيَتْ فِي رُومَا، حَيْثُ⁩ : ⁧المُوَظَّفَة⁩

fī Rūmā, ḥayṯu ġayyarta ṭ-ṭāʾira. you know- in Rome, where you changed your plane. ⁧غَيَّرْتَ الطَّائِرَةَ. سَتَصِلُ غَدًا عَلَى الأَرْجَحِ.⁩ taṣilu ġadan ʿalā l-arǧaḥ. uktub hunā He'll probably be here tomorrow. ʿunwānaka wa-raqma hātifik, wa-sa- Write your address and your address here ⁧اُكْتُبْ هُنَا عُنْوَانَكَ وَرَقْمَ هَاتِفِكَ، وَسَنُرْسِلُهَا⁩ nursiluhā Ilayk. Phone number, and we'll send it to you.

rows: ⁧لُوكَا: شُكْرًا. هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ تُعْطِيَنِي رَقْمًا لِلْمُتَابَعَةِ؟⁩
Lūkā: šukran. hal yumkinu an tuʿṭiyanī raqman li-l-mutābaʿa?
Thank you. Can you give me a practice number to follow her?

blocks.text: al-muwaẓẓafa: ṭabʿan, hāḏā raqmu l- The employee: Of course, this is the
⁧طَبْعًا، هٰذَا رَقْمُ البَلَاغِ. احْتَفِظْ بِهِ.⁩ : ⁧المُوَظَّفَة⁩

balāġ. iḥtafiẓ Bih. Report number. Keep it. What to notice. ⁧سَبَبُ الزِّيَارَةِ⁩ • the reason for the visit • ⁧كَمْ يَوْمًا⁩ ( A2-12), ⁧سَتُقِيمُ⁩ • will stay ( ⁧أَقَامَ⁩ , IV concave). ⁧لَوْ سَمَحْتَ⁩ Excuse me, please. "If you allow": a very used courteous formula. ⁧قَسِيمَةُ الأَمْتِعَةِ⁩ The baggage receipt is included. ⁧صِفْ لِي⁩ ( A2-15). ⁧حَيْثُ⁩ Where the place is located. ⁧عَلَى الأَرْجَحِ⁩ It's probably not. ⁧اِحْتَفِظْ بِهِ⁩ (VIII). ⁧بَلَاغ⁩ • Complaint, alert • The blue suitcase is that of A2-11, the heaviest one in the world... Luke arrived via Rome.
2. Ask with courtesy

rows: I'd like to book a room.
Can I pay with the card?

blocks.text: … ⁧أَوَدُّ أَنْ⁩ formal ... ⁧أَوَدُّ أَنْ أَسْأَلَ عَنْ⁩ I'd like to ask for information about...

To answer a request: ⁧تَفَضَّلْ⁩ / ⁧تَفَضَّلِي⁩ Please, here you are. ⁧طَبْعًا⁩ , ⁧بِكُلِّ سُرُورٍ⁩ ( A2-04), ⁧مَعَ الأَسَفِ⁩ Unfortunately, it does not. ⁧لَحْظَةً⁩ ( A2-10). To thank in a formal way: ⁧شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا⁩ , ⁧أَشْكُرُكَ عَلَى مُسَاعَدَتِكَ⁩ .
3. At the airport
⁧تَذْكِرَةُ ذَهَابٍ وَإِيَابٍ⁩ Round trip ticket

The questions to passport control are almost always the same: ⁧مَا سَبَبُ الزِّيَارَةِ؟⁩ · ⁧كَمْ يَوْمًا سَتَبْقَى؟⁩ · ⁧أَيْنَ سَتُقِيمُ؟⁩ · ⁧هَلْ عِنْدَكَ تَأْشِيرَةٌ؟⁩ · ⁧مَا مِهْنَتُكَ؟⁩ Answer with short and precise phrases.
4. At the hotel and in transport

rows: ⁧أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَحْجِزَ غُرْفَةً لِشَخْصَيْنِ مِنْ ١٣ إِلَى ١٦ يُولْيُو.⁩
⁧اِمْلَأْ هٰذِهِ البِطَاقَةَ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ: الاسْمُ، الجِنْسِيَّةُ، رَقْمُ الجَوَازِ.⁩
⁧فِي الغُرْفَةِ ضَجِيجٌ.⁩ · ⁧لَا يُوجَدُ مَاءٌ سَاخِنٌ.⁩ · ⁧المُكَيِّفُ لَا يَعْمَلُ.⁩
⁧هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ أَتْرُكَ الحَقِيبَةَ هُنَا حَتَّى المَسَاءِ؟⁩ · ⁧أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَدْفَعَ الحِسَابَ.⁩
⁧قِفْ هُنَا، لَوْ سَمَحْتَ.⁩ · ⁧إِلَى الدُّقِّي، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. كَمِ الأُجْرَةُ؟⁩
⁧تَذْكِرَةٌ إِلَى الإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّةِ، ذَهَابٌ فَقَطْ.⁩ · ⁧أَيْنَ مَحَطَّةُ المِتْرُو؟⁩

blocks.text: Culture. In many Arab countries, as in Italy, hotels record data of foreign guests from the passport: keep the document at hand. In taxis without taximeter the price is agreed before (A2-14).
5. Dialogue 2 · By the doctor Manṣūr
Wednesday night, third day of class. Luke is not well; Ṭāriq He's taking him to the doctor. Manṣūr, a doctor from the neighborhood.

rows: Please sit down. What's wrong with him?
⁧لُوكَا: عِنْدِي أَلَمٌ فِي البَطْنِ، وَأَشْعُرُ بِتَعَبٍ شَدِيدٍ.⁩
Lūkā: ʿindī alamun fī l-baṭn, wa-ašʿuru bi-taʿabin šadīd.
Luca: I have a stomachache and I feel very tired.
⁧لُوكَا: مُنْذُ أَمْسِ. فِي اللَّيْلِ كَانَ عِنْدِي صُدَاعٌ وَحَرَارَةٌ خَفِيفَةٌ.⁩
Lūkā: munḏu ams. fī l-layli kāna ʿindī ṣudāʿun wa-ḥarāratun ḫafīfa.
Since yesterday. Tonight I had a headache and a fever.
The doctor: What did you eat yesterday?
⁧أَكَلْتُ فِي الشَّارِعِ مَعَ زُمَلَائِي فِي⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧وَشَرِبْتُ عَصِيرًا بِالثَّلْجِ.⁩ … ⁧الدَّوْرَةِ⁩
Lūkā: akaltu fī š-šāriʿi maʿa zumalāʾī fī d-dawra… wa-šaribtu ʿaṣīran bi-ṯ-ṯalǧ.
I ate on the street with my classmates and drank a juice with ice.
⁧لَا تَقْلَقْ، الأَمْرُ⁩ ( ⁧بَعْدَ الفَحْصِ⁩ ) ⁧الطَّبِيب:⁩ ⁧بَسِيطٌ. هٰذَا يَحْدُثُ كَثِيرًا لِلزُّوَّارِ فِي الصَّيْفِ.⁩ ⁧هَلْ عِنْدَكَ حَسَاسِيَّةٌ مِنْ أَيِّ دَوَاءٍ؟⁩
aṭ-ṭabīb: (baʿda l-faḥṣ) lā taqlaq, al- amru basīṭ. hāḏā yaḥduṯu kaṯīran li-z- zuwwāri fī ṣ-ṣayf. hal ʿindaka ḥasāsiyyatun min ayyi dawāʾ?
Your doctor: (after your visit) Don't worry, it's a simple thing. It often happens to visitors in summer. Do you have allergies to any medications?
⁧الطَّبِيب: سَأَكْتُبُ لَكَ وَصْفَةً. خُذْ قُرْصًا بَعْدَ الأَكْلِ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ فِي اليَوْمِ، وَاشْرَبْ مَاءً كَثِيرًا. وَلَا تَأْكُلْ فِي الشَّارِعِ هٰذَا الأُسْبُوعَ!⁩
aṭ-ṭabīb: sa-aktubu laka waṣfa. ḫuḏ qurṣan baʿda l-akli ṯalāṯa marrātin fī l- yawm, wa-šrab māʾan kaṯīrā. wa-lā taʾkul fī š-šāriʿi hāḏā l-usbūʿ!
The doctor: I'll write you a recipe. Take one tablet after meals three times a day and drink plenty of water. And you're not eating on the street this week!
⁧لُوكَا: وَهَلْ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَذْهَبَ إِلَى الدَّوْرَةِ غَدًا؟⁩
Lūkā: wa-hal astaṭīʿu an aḏhaba ilā d- dawrati ġadā?
Luca: And tomorrow I can go to the course?
⁧الطَّبِيب: إِذَا لَمْ تَكُنْ عِنْدَكَ حَرَارَةٌ، فَنَعَمْ. وَإِذَا لَمْ تَتَحَسَّنْ بَعْدَ يَوْمَيْنِ، فَارْجِعْ إِلَيَّ.⁩
aṭ-ṭabīb: iḏā lam takun ʿindaka ḥarāra, fa-naʿam. wa-iḏā lam tataḥassan baʿda yawmayn, fa-rǧiʿ ilayya.
Your doctor: If you do not have a fever, yes. And if you don't get better in two days, come back to me.
Ṭāriq: (fī š-šāriʿ) a-raʾayt? al-āna taʿrifu kalimāti ṭ-ṭibbi ayḍā!
Ṭāriq: (on the street) Did you see? Now you know the words of medicine!

blocks.text: What to notice. ⁧مِمَّ تَشْكُو؟⁩ What does he complain about? ⁧مِنْ⁩ + ⁧مَا⁩ → ⁧مِمَّ⁩ ; A2-13, A2-15) is the doctor's typical question. ⁧عِنْدِي أَلَمٌ فِي⁩ I'm sick at... ⁧أَشْعُرُ بِـ⁩ ( A2-19), ⁧مُنْذُ مَتَى؟⁩ Since when? ⁧حَرَارَة⁩ this is ⁧حُمَّى⁩ ). ⁧عَصِير⁩ • juice • • juice • juice • juice • juice ⁧ثَلْج⁩ Ice. ⁧الفَحْص⁩ The visit will be done. ⁧يَتَحَسَّنُ⁩ • improve (V). ⁧أَرَأَيْتَ؟⁩ = ⁧هَلْ رَأَيْتَ؟⁩ ( ⁧أَ⁩ Interrogative). The doctor's instructions are an example of dialogue: the recipe and the leaflet are valid for a real drug.
6. To the doctor and pharmacy

Telling where it hurts. ⁧عِنْدِي أَلَمٌ فِي⁩ + body part, or: ⁧يُؤْلِمُنِي⁩ + body part (Lett. It hurts... ⁧يُؤْلِمُنِي رَأْسِي⁩ My head hurts. ⁧تُؤْلِمُنِي مَعِدَتِي⁩ , ⁧تُؤْلِمُنِي رِجْلِي⁩ (the female body parts, as ⁧رِجْل⁩ and ⁧يَد⁩ , they want ⁧تُؤْلِمُ⁩ ).
The doctor's questions. ⁧مِمَّ تَشْكُو؟⁩ · ⁧أَيْنَ يُؤْلِمُكَ؟⁩ · ⁧مُنْذُ مَتَى؟⁩ · ⁧هَلْ عِنْدَكَ حَرَارَةٌ؟⁩ · ⁧هَلْ تَأْخُذُ أَدْوِيَةً؟⁩ · ⁧هَلْ عِنْدَكَ⁩
⁧حَسَاسِيَّةٌ؟⁩

To the pharmacy. ⁧أُرِيدُ دَوَاءً لِلصُّدَاعِ⁩ . · ⁧هَلْ أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى وَصْفَةٍ؟⁩ · ⁧كَمْ قُرْصًا آخُذُ فِي اليَوْمِ؟⁩ · ⁧قَبْلَ الأَكْلِ أَمْ بَعْدَهُ؟⁩ In Arab countries, pharmacists often give advice (A2-14); prescription drugs are bought with the ⁧وَصْفَة⁩ . Written instructions (recognize): ⁧يُؤْخَذُ⁩ • take • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • ⁧قُرْصٌ وَاحِدٌ كُلَّ ثَمَانِي سَاعَاتٍ⁩ 1 tablet every eight hours. ⁧لَا يُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلْأَطْفَالِ⁩ Do not use for children. ⁧يُحْفَظُ بَعِيدًا عَنْ مُتَنَاوَلِ الأَطْفَالِ⁩ Keep out of the reach of children. They are passive (A2-17).

rows: ⁧مُنْتَهِي الصَّلَاحِيَّةِ⁩ · … ⁧الجَوَازُ صَالِحٌ حَتَّى⁩ · ⁧نُسْخَةٌ مِنَ الجَوَازِ⁩ · ⁧صُورَةٌ شَخْصِيَّةٌ⁩
⁧كَمِ الرُّسُومُ؟⁩ ( A2-12) · ⁧هَلْ أَدْفَعُ هُنَا أَمْ فِي شُبَّاكٍ آخَرَ؟⁩
⁧اُكْتُبْهُ لِي، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.⁩ · ⁧لَمْ أَفْهَمْ، هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ تُعِيدَ؟⁩

blocks.text: 8. Pronunciation

law samaḥt. Two related words: law-sa-maḥt, with ḥ Faringale. alam, ṣudāʿ, ḥummā. Attention to the emphatic and faringal consonants: ṣ of ṣudāʿ, ḥ of ḥummā and ḥasāsiyya. yuʾlimunī. The hamza in the middle: yuʾ-li-mu-nī.
9. New lexicon
★ ⁧أَمْتِعَة⁩ amtiʿa baggage ⁧م ت ع⁩ name (pl.) sing. ⁧مَتَاع⁩

rows: m. · pl. ⁧أَدْوَار⁩ · ⁧دَوْرُكَ⁩ The next step is yours.

blocks.text: Notes of use. ⁧إِقَامَة⁩ is the "living room" ( ⁧مُدَّةُ الإِقَامَةِ⁩ (a) the duration of the stay is not less than 30 days, but also the residence permit is not less than 30 days. ⁧تَصْرِيحُ الإِقَامَةِ⁩ , in the Gulf simply ⁧الإِقَامَة⁩ ). ⁧أَمْتِعَة⁩ is a plural (the singular ⁧مَتَاع⁩ it is rare): ⁧أَمْتِعَتِي⁩ My luggage is in the bag. ⁧شُبَّاك⁩ is both the window (especially in the Levant and Egypt) and the door: ⁧شُبَّاكُ التَّذَاكِرِ⁩ Ticket office. ⁧دَوْر⁩ : + turn ( ⁧اِنْتَظِرْ دَوْرَكَ⁩ ) and () role ( ⁧دَوْرُ الشُّرْطَةِ⁩ ). ⁧وَصْفَة⁩ is the prescription of your doctor ( ⁧وَصْفَةٌ طِبِّيَّةٌ⁩ ) and the kitchen. ⁧صَالِح⁩ also means "good," suitable for: ⁧صَالِحٌ لِلشُّرْبِ⁩ Drinking is not allowed.
10. Examples in context

rows: My flight was cancelled due to the bad weather.
When do I pick up my bags?
My hand's been hurting since I fell.
hal aḥtāǧu ilā waṣfatin li-hāḏā d- dawāʾ?
Do I need a prescription for this medicine?
ǧawāzī ṣāliḥun ḥattā ʿāmi alfayni wa- ṯalāṯīn.
urīdu an uǧaddida l-iqāma. mā l- awrāqu l-maṭlūba?

law samaḥt, hal hāḏā āḫiru ṭ-ṭābūr?

Exercise 1 · With courtesy

Transform into courteous requests ( ⁧هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ⁩ … / ⁧لَوْ سَمَحْتَ⁩ / ⁧أَرْجُو أَنْ⁩ …): a) ⁧أَعْطِنِي المِفْتَاحَ⁩ . · b) ⁧أُرِيدُ غُرْفَةً هَادِئَةً⁩ . · c) ⁧غَيِّرْ مَقْعَدِي⁩ . · d) ⁧أَرْسِلُوا لِي الفَاتُورَةَ⁩ (Invoices) (written) · e) ⁧اُكْتُبِ العُنْوَانَ⁩ . · f) ⁧قِفْ هُنَا⁩ .
Exercise 2 · At the airport

Answer passport control questions with full sentences: a) ⁧مَا سَبَبُ الزِّيَارَةِ؟⁩ · b) ⁧كَمْ يَوْمًا سَتَبْقَى؟⁩ · c) ⁧أَيْنَ سَتُقِيمُ؟⁩ · d) ⁧مَا مِهْنَتُكَ؟⁩ · e) ⁧هَلْ هٰذِهِ زِيَارَتُكَ الأُولَى؟⁩
Exercise 3 · At the hotel

Write the customer's lines: a) has a reservation in your name · b) asks if breakfast is included · c) says the air conditioning doesn't work · d) asks to leave the suitcase until evening · e) He wants to pay the bill with the card
Exercise 4 · By the doctor
Write down what you would say: a) you have three days headache · b) your leg hurts · c) you have a cough and a little fever ·
d) you are allergic to penicillin ( ⁧البِنِسِلِين⁩ ) · e) ask how many tablets to take per day · f) Ask if you can work tomorrow
Exercise 5 · At the pharmacy

Complete the dialog: ⁧الزَّبُون⁩ : ⁧◌⁩ (I would like a cough medication). — ⁧الصَّيْدَلِيّ⁩ : ⁧هَلْ عِنْدَكَ حَرَارَةٌ؟⁩ — ⁧الزَّبُون⁩ : ⁧◌⁩ (No, but my throat hurts.) — ⁧الصَّيْدَلِيّ⁩ : ⁧خُذْ هٰذَا، مِلْعَقَةً⁩ (Spokes) (spokes) ⁧ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ فِي اليَوْمِ⁩ . — ⁧الزَّبُون⁩ : ⁧◌⁩ (before or after meals?) ⁧الصَّيْدَلِيّ⁩ : ⁧بَعْدَ الأَكْلِ⁩ . — ⁧الزَّبُون⁩ : ⁧◌⁩ (Do you need a recipe?)
Exercise 6 · At the door
Translate: a) Where's the end of the line? · b) My turn? · c) I'd like to renew my passport. · d) What documents do you need? · e) My passport has expired. · f) When do I get my card?
Exercise 7 · Lost baggage
Write a five-line description of your bag (or backpack) for the lost luggage office: color, size, material, special signs ( ⁧عَلَامَاتٌ مُمَيَّزَةٌ⁩ ), contained.
Exercise 8 · Translate
a) The flight is two hours late. · b) I'd like a seat by the window. · c) The doctor gave me a prescription. · d)
I need a visa insurance. · e) The flight to Rome has been cancelled. · f) My stomach's been hurting since last night.

a) ⁧يُؤْلِمُنِي يَدِي⁩ · b) ⁧عِنْدِي أَلَمٌ عَلَى رَأْسِي⁩ · c) ⁧هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ تُسَاعِدُنِي؟⁩ · d) ⁧أُرِيدُ أَنَّ أَحْجِزَ⁩ · e) ⁧الجَوَازُ صَالِحَةٌ⁩ · f) ⁧مُنْذُ مَتَى⁩

Exercise 11 · Understanding

A) What data does the card ask for? Which ones are related to the passport? What are the reasons for the visit? Fill in the card with Luca's data (invents what is missing). B) a) What is the drug for? b) How many tablets a day, and how many hours? c) How do you take it? d) Who doesn't have to use it? e) When should you consult your doctor? f) How do you store it?
13. Writing
Exercise 12 · Booking by email (week 86)

Write an email of about 80 words, vocalized, to a hotel in Alexandria (invented) to book a room for two nights at the end of the course: dates, type of room, breakfast, price, arrival late in the evening, a question about parking or transportation from the station. Compulsory elements: a formal opening and closing formula (A2-22 deepens them: for now ⁧السَّيِّدُ المُدِيرُ المُحْتَرَمُ⁩ / ⁧تَحِيَّةً طَيِّبَةً⁩ and ⁧مَعَ الشُّكْرِ وَالتَّقْدِيرِ⁩ ), ⁧أُرِيدُ أَنْ⁩ / ⁧أَوَدُّ أَنْ⁩ , ⁧هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ⁩ , ⁧أَرْجُو أَنْ⁩ .
Exercise 13 · Fill out a form (week 87)

Fill in the reading record sheet 2 with your data (or invented data), in Arabic; then write five sentences to say at the counter to renew a document: what do you want, what documents you have, ask for the cost and times, ask to repeat.
14. Listening
Script A · Dialogues 1 and 2
Listen to the two dialogues without reading them and answer questions a) and b) for the year 14.
Script B · At the airport
Announcements and short exchanges invented.
⁧١. سَيِّدَاتِي وَسَادَتِي، نَرْجُو مِنَ المُسَافِرِينَ عَلَى الرِّحْلَةِ رَقْمِ ثَلَاثِمِئَةٍ وَأَرْبَعَةٍ المُتَّجِهَةِ إِلَى مِيلَانُو⁩
⁧التَّوَجُّهَ إِلَى البَوَّابَةِ رَقْمِ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ.⁩

Exercise 14 · Applications

a) Dialogue 1: what does the agent ask and what does Luke answer? What's wrong with Luca after that? How he describes The suitcase? Where did she stay and when will she arrive? What does Luke receive in the end? b) Dialogue 2: what symptoms does Luca have and since when? What did you eat and drink? What does your doctor prescribe? Can you go to the class? When does he have to come back? c) Script B: for each ad or exchange write the main information (flight number, exit, weight, place, time). d) Script C: what does Luca want, what is missing, where he has to go, what should he bring, when he receives the card, what advantages does the card give?
15. Oral production

1. Manage a trip (week) 86). Playing with the tutor in three scenes: check-in at the airport (place, baggage weight), passport control, arrival at the hotel (booking, breakfast, a problem in the room).

2. From the doctor and to the desk (session, week 87). The tutor does the doctor: describe two disorders (where, from when, how), answer his questions, ask how to take the medicine. Then he becomes an employee: you have to renew a document; ask what it takes, how much it costs and when it's ready.
3. Lost luggage. Tell an employee your suitcase didn't arrive and describe it.
